Real-Prompt Controlled Replay Master Report

This is the controlled real-prompt version of the master report. The prompts come from real SWE-bench / DeepAgents traces, while the experiment controls tool-wait time, cache pressure, and direct KV prefetch timing.

Use this report for the clean hardware-story experiment: real prompt content, known resume deadlines, known pressure levels, direct SGLang KV-hook attempts, and replay-side KV movement evidence.

Experiment Setup And Manager Summary

This milestone keeps real SWE-bench/DeepAgents prompt content, but controls the timing. That gives us a cleaner hardware-style experiment: same kind of agent text, known wait windows, known cache pressure, and direct SGLang KV-hook attempts.

part simple meaning
1. Real prompt pair Use two adjacent model turns from real AgentBench/DeepAgents traces.
2. Controlled wait Replay Turn A, then impose a chosen tool-wait window such as 100 ms or 500 ms.
3. Cache pressure Send filler requests during the wait to make KV residency harder.
4. Direct KV hint In prefetch modes, issue the marked direct-load request during the wait.
5. Resume Send Turn B at the scheduled resume time, even if the hint is still running.

Global Prefetch Margin

Positive margin means the hint path finished before replay. Negative margin means replay arrived first.

This chart compresses every matched live prefetch attempt into one dot. The y-axis is the prefetch margin: positive means the prefetch finished before the resume request; negative means it finished after the agent already resumed.

How To Read The Timelines

Purple means the prefetch attempt ran. Green means that attempt had attributed direct KV host-to-device movement. Cyan means the replay request itself loaded KV from host to GPU. Magenta means replay likely rebuilt missing prefix/KV work. Gold is the remaining before-first-token work. Purple without green means the hint ran, but no matching HtoD load was observed for that displayed gap.

The timeline uses a symlog full-replay view. It compresses very long replay requests so red bars can extend to their true end while the important activity around 0 ms remains visible.

The report may also include a Readable Phase Timeline. That view removes the global time axis: each phase gets a fixed readable column, and the true duration is printed on the bar.

One Row In Plain English

Each timeline row is one tool-wait episode: model turn, tool call, wait, optional prefetch, then model resume.

step timeline color simple meaning
1. Ask model what to do blue bar model turn before the tool call
2. Model says to call a tool end of blue bar the model turn hands work to a tool
3. Tool runs gray bar read_file(), grep(), run_tests(), etc. is happening
4. Agent waits gray bar this wait is the prefetch opportunity
5. Tool returns black vertical line the next model turn is due
6. Agent asks model again red bar resume request after the tool result
Before the replay produces its first token gold, cyan, or magenta bar time-before-first-token work; gold is normal remaining prefill/wait, cyan is host KV load, magenta is recompute/rebuild
During steps 3/4, if prefetch is enabled purple bar our software prefetch attempt runs during the wait
Inside the purple window, if KV moved green bar direct SGLang KV host-to-device movement was observed for that hint
Inside the red replay request, if KV moved cyan bar the real replay request itself performed host-to-device KV movement

Color Legend

color meaning simple description
blue Initial model turn The agent asks the model what to do next. This request may produce a tool call such as read_file(), grep(), edit_file(), or execute().
gray Tool wait window The tool or harness is running, so the model is idle for this session. This pause is the opportunity to prepare that session's KV before the agent resumes.
purple Prefetch attempt window This includes detecting that the tool call finished, creating a hint for that agent/session, calling our direct SGLang KV hook, letting SGLang check whether host-side KV exists, and if needed, asking SGLang to move KV back to GPU memory.
green Direct KV host-to-device movement This is evidence that KV load/copy work was observed for the hint. In simple words: this is the closest timeline bar to 'KV pages were brought back toward GPU memory'.
cyan Replay-side KV host-to-device movement This is evidence from the normal replay request path. It means the resumed request itself had to move KV from host-side memory toward GPU memory while serving the real agent turn.
black Replay due boundary This is when the tool result is ready and the next model turn should be able to start. If purple or green finishes after this line, the prefetch path was late for that resume.
red Replay decode The agent asks the model to continue after the tool result. In the controlled timeline, red starts after first token and mostly means normal generation/decoding.
gold Normal replay prefill / wait This is the remaining time before first token after visible host-load and recompute evidence is separated out. It can include queueing, prefix matching, and normal new-token processing.
magenta Replay recompute / rebuild This means replay likely rebuilt missing prefix/KV work instead of cleanly loading the old KV from host memory.

Replay Path Proof Table

This is the main evidence ledger. Each row explains what happened when the replay request resumed: whether it reused cache, loaded KV from host to GPU, recomputed missing tokens, or mostly waited in the scheduler/request path.

Confidence matters. High confidence means the row has direct SGLang evidence plus HtoD movement evidence. Medium confidence means SGLang counters support the label. Low confidence means the label still depends mostly on TTFT and timeline shape.

matched_prefix_tokens means the first cache match visible when replay started. final_cached_prefix_tokens means how much prefix existed later after replay/cache work progressed. A large difference between them is evidence of replay-side prefill/recompute work, not a clean cache hit.

Replay Path Attribution

This section turns the segmented TTFT window into stronger evidence. For each replay, it reports SGLang prefix/cache counters observed inside the replay window: prompt tokens, cached prefix tokens, estimated new prefill tokens, host-hit tokens, host-load tokens, and replay-side HtoD events.

The verdict is evidence-backed but still conservative. Initial cached-prefix tokens show what was reusable when replay began. Final cached-prefix tokens show what existed later after replay work. A cyan bar plus host-load tokens is stronger proof that replay loaded KV from host to GPU.

Mixed Timeline Sample / Deadline Timeline

This is the deadline view. The black line is when replay was due. This view is best for seeing whether the purple prefetch attempt finished before the deadline.

Timeline Model

Timeline ElementColor StripMeaning
Initial model turnFirst model request before tool wait
Tool waitAgent/tool pause where prefetch could happen
Direct prefetch attemptOur hint/direct-load path tried to prepare KV
Hint-side KV HtoDPrefetch path actually loaded KV from host to GPU
Replay-side KV HtoDReplay itself loaded KV from host to GPU
Replay recomputeReplay rebuilt missing old KV/prefix tokens
Normal replay prefillSmall remaining prefill/new-token processing before first token
Replay decodeGeneration after first token
Replay dueDeadline when KV should ideally already be ready

Readable Phase Timeline

This view keeps readable phase columns, but each column has its own local timing. In simple words: the bars inside prefetch are positioned relative to the prefetch attempt, and the bars inside replay path are positioned relative to the replay request.

Replay work is split into separate lanes: cyan means replay-side KV HtoD, magenta means recompute/rebuild, gold means remaining before-first-token work, and red means decode after first token.

Timeline Model

Timeline ElementColor StripMeaning
Initial model turnFirst model request before tool wait
Tool waitAgent/tool pause where prefetch could happen
Direct prefetch attemptOur hint/direct-load path tried to prepare KV
Hint-side KV HtoDPrefetch path actually loaded KV from host to GPU
Replay-side KV HtoDReplay itself loaded KV from host to GPU
Replay recomputeReplay rebuilt missing old KV/prefix tokens
Normal replay prefillSmall remaining prefill/new-token processing before first token
Replay decodeGeneration after first token
Replay dueDeadline when KV should ideally already be ready

KV Lifecycle Evidence

This section follows the KV lifecycle for the same rows shown in the timeline. It answers five simple questions for each tool gap:

  1. Did SGLang write this session's KV to host HiCache?
  2. Was that KV evicted from GPU memory?
  3. Was the host copy also evicted?
  4. Did prefetch or replay load the old KV back from host to GPU?
  5. If not, did replay have to rebuild/prefill missing KV?

The simple_meaning column is the fastest way to read this table. Example: if host write, GPU eviction, and host eviction are all nonzero, but replay H2D is zero and replay only matched a tiny prefix, then the old KV was lost and replay rebuilt/prefilled.

Column Legend

field simple meaning
host_write_tokens SGLang copied this session's KV from GPU memory into host HiCache.
gpu_evict_tokens SGLang removed this session's KV from GPU memory.
host_evict_tokens SGLang also removed this session's host-side HiCache copy.
hint_h2d_tokens The prefetch attempt loaded KV from host back to GPU.
replay_h2d_tokens The real replay request loaded KV from host back to GPU.
replay_initial_match_tokens How much prefix/KV SGLang could reuse when replay first arrived.
replay_new_prefill_tokens Estimated tokens replay had to rebuild/prefill because they were not immediately reusable.

This section tracks logical KV blocks across SGLang cache events. It is more detailed than the timeline: each block has a stable ledger row showing whether it was written to host, evicted from GPU, evicted from host, or loaded back.

This is logical block tracking, not a physical GPU page snooper. The ledger uses SGLang node IDs when available and nearby token-range matching when node IDs are missing.

Timeline ElementColor StripMeaning
Initial model turnFirst model request before tool wait

Replay-side KV HtoDReplay itself loaded KV from host to GPU

Normal replay prefillSmall remaining prefill/new-token processing before first token
Replay decodeGeneration after first token
Replay dueDeadline when KV should ideally already be ready

Reproduce This Report

Use one script to generate this master report. It can run the controlled replay experiment, the live AgentBench direct-prefetch experiment, or both.

Run The Full Master Report

cd ~/agentic_hardware/sglang_direct_kv
source .venv/bin/activate

EXPERIMENT_KIND=controlled \
REPORT_LABEL=controlled_demo_1 \
PRESSURE_PROFILE=high \
UPDATE_LATEST=1 \
MAX_TIMELINE_GAPS=18 \
TRACE_INDEX_CSV=~/kv_cache_offloading/experiments/reports/latest_prompt_evolution_trace_index.csv \
MODES="no_prefetch direct_prefetch" \
TOOL_WAIT_LIST_MS="100 250 500 1000" \
FILLER_LIST="32 64 128" \
REQUEST_CONCURRENCY=8 \
MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS=12288 \
HICACHE_SIZE_GB=8 \
MEM_FRACTION_STATIC=0.75 \
bash scripts/run_master_report.sh \
  Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct

Output:

artifacts/results/latest_master_report.html
artifacts/results/reports/controlled_demo_1/master_report.html
artifacts/results/latest_manifest.json

Rebuild From Existing Runs

Use this when experiments already ran and you only want to regenerate the HTML, tables, timelines, and global prefetch-margin dot charts.

cd ~/agentic_hardware/sglang_direct_kv
source .venv/bin/activate

BUILD_ONLY=1 \
EXPERIMENT_KIND=controlled \
REPORT_LABEL=controlled_demo_1_rebuild \
UPDATE_LATEST=0 \
CONTROLLED_ROOT=artifacts/results/runs/controlled/controlled_demo_1 \
bash scripts/run_master_report.sh \
  Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct

Preview Before Running

cd ~/agentic_hardware/sglang_direct_kv
source .venv/bin/activate

DRY_RUN=1 \
EXPERIMENT_KIND=controlled \
REPORT_LABEL=controlled_demo_1 \
bash scripts/run_master_report.sh \
  Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct

Important Knobs

knob meaning
EXPERIMENT_KIND controlled, live, or both
PRESSURE_PROFILE custom, low, medium, high, or extreme
REPORT_LABEL folder name for this run under artifacts/results/reports/
UPDATE_LATEST 1 replaces artifacts/results/latest_master_report.html
BUILD_ONLY 1 rebuilds HTML from existing run folders
DRY_RUN 1 prints what would run without launching SGLang
MAX_TIMELINE_GAPS number of rows shown in each timeline
START_INDEX / END_INDEX AgentBench task range for live runs
WORKLOAD_JSONL / TRACE_INDEX_CSV real prompt-pair source for controlled replay

Pressure Profiles

Use PRESSURE_PROFILE when you want to deliberately increase cache pressure and request pressure. Manual environment variables still override the profile defaults.

profile controlled pressure live pressure
low 4 prompt pairs, fillers 8/16, concurrency 2 tasks 0-3, max steps 6
medium 8 prompt pairs, fillers 16/32, concurrency 4 tasks 0-15, max steps 10
high 16 prompt pairs, fillers 32/64/128, concurrency 8 tasks 0-31, max steps 10
extreme 24 prompt pairs, fillers 64/128/192, concurrency 12 tasks 0-63, max steps 15
custom use only the knobs you explicitly set use only the knobs you explicitly set
